---
title: "Working with fitted results"
description: "Choose an estimator, inspect its result, compare models, and find the next operation."
sidebar: reference
---

An estimation function returns a fitted result. Use its methods to inspect or
analyze the fit, and package functions such as `pf.etable()` to compare results.
Each result's supported operations are described in the [model support table](/reference-guide/model-support.qmd).

## Choose an estimator

| Model | Function | Single-fit result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Linear regression with optional absorbed fixed effects | [`pf.feols()`](/reference/estimation.api.feols.feols.qmd) | [`Feols`](/reference/estimation.models.feols_.Feols.qmd) |
| Instrumental variables and 2SLS | [`pf.feols()`](/reference/estimation.api.feols.feols.qmd), using `[endogenous ~ instruments]` | [`Feiv`](/reference/estimation.models.feiv_.Feiv.qmd) |
| Poisson regression | [`pf.fepois()`](/reference/estimation.api.fepois.fepois.qmd) | [`Fepois`](/reference/estimation.models.fepois_.Fepois.qmd) |
| Logit, probit, Gaussian, or Poisson GLM | [`pf.feglm()`](/reference/estimation.api.feglm.feglm.qmd), with `family=` | A family-specific GLM result |
| Conditional quantiles | [`pf.quantreg()`](/reference/estimation.api.quantreg.quantreg.qmd) | [`Quantreg`](/reference/estimation.quantreg.quantreg_.Quantreg.qmd); absorbed fixed effects are unsupported |

```{python}
import pyfixest as pf

data = pf.get_data(N=200, seed=1234)
fit = pf.feols("Y ~ X1 + X2 | f1", data, vcov={"CRV1": "f1"})
fit.tidy()
```

## Inspect one fit

| Task | Access |
| --- | --- |
| Coefficients and coefficient-level inference as a DataFrame | [`fit.tidy()`](/reference/estimation.models.feols_.Feols.tidy.qmd) |
| Named estimates, standard errors, statistics, or p-values | [`fit.coef()`](/reference/estimation.models.feols_.Feols.coef.qmd), [`fit.se()`](/reference/estimation.models.feols_.Feols.se.qmd), [`fit.tstat()`](/reference/estimation.models.feols_.Feols.tstat.qmd), [`fit.pvalue()`](/reference/estimation.models.feols_.Feols.pvalue.qmd) |
| Confidence intervals | [`fit.confint(alpha=0.05)`](/reference/estimation.models.feols_.Feols.confint.qmd); `alpha` is the significance level |
| Goodness of fit | [`fit.fitstat`](/reference/estimation.state.FitStatistics.qmd); undefined measures are `NaN` |
| Sample size and dropped observations | [`fit.sample_info`](/reference/estimation.state.EstimationSample.qmd) |
| Formula and estimator description | [`fit.model`](/reference/estimation.state.ModelDescription.qmd) |
| Estimation options | [`fit.options`](/reference/estimation.state.EstimationOptions.qmd) |
| Covariance matrix and its specification | [`fit.variance_covariance`](/reference/estimation.state.VarianceCovariance.qmd) |
| IV first-stage fit and diagnostics | [`fit.first_stage`](/reference/estimation.state.FirstStage.qmd); [`fit.IV_Diag()`](/reference/estimation.models.feiv_.Feiv.IV_Diag.qmd) |

Methods have parentheses; attributes do not. For example, `fit.coef()` returns
a Series, whereas `fit.fitstat` is a component whose fields include `rmse` and
`r2`. The full [state reference](/reference/index.qmd#fitted-state) describes
the more detailed components.

```{python}
fit.fitstat.rmse, fit.sample_info.n_rows, fit.model.formula
```

## Predict and change inference

[`fit.predict()`](/reference/estimation.models.feols_.Feols.predict.qmd) returns
in-sample predictions in retained estimation-row order. To align with a new
frame, supply `newdata=`; missing covariate values and unsupported unseen levels
produce missing predictions. GLM offsets have stricter validation: a missing
offset value raises `ValueError`.
For GLMs the current default is the linear predictor: use `type="response"`
explicitly for response-scale means or probabilities.

```{python}
fit.predict(newdata=data.head())
```

[`fit.vcov()`](/reference/estimation.models.feols_.Feols.vcov.qmd) changes
inference **in place** and returns the same result. It does not refit the
coefficients. Check model and storage support before changing covariance.

```{python}
fit.vcov("HC1").tidy()
```

[`fit.fixef()`](/reference/estimation.models.feols_.Feols.fixef.qmd) recovers
absorbed effects on supported fits and creates `fit.fixef_estimates`.
Individual levels depend on the stated normalization; GLM effects are on the
link scale.

## Work with several fits

Multiple formulas, sample splits, and quantile lists can return
[`FixestMulti`](/reference/estimation.FixestMulti_.FixestMulti.qmd). Inspect its
combined tables, extract one result, or pass the collection to reporting tools.

```{python}
models = pf.feols("Y ~ sw(X1, X2)", data)
models.tidy()
```

```{python}
first = models.fetch_model(0, print_fml=False)
first.coef()
```

`models.to_list()` returns the fitted objects in container order. A container
can hold different result subclasses; extraction does not turn them into OLS.

## Tables and plots

| Task | Function | Return and next step |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Print regression summaries | [`pf.summary()`](/reference/report.summary.qmd) or `fit.summary()` | Printed summary |
| Compare estimates in a table | [`pf.etable()`](/reference/report.etable.qmd) | Choose `type=` for a table object, data, text, or a file format |
| Compare selected coefficients across specifications | [`pf.coefplot()`](/reference/report.coefplot.qmd) | Matplotlib Figure or Lets-Plot object according to `plot_backend=` |
| Plot terms generated by `i()` | [`pf.iplot()`](/reference/report.iplot.qmd) | Same backend choice; ordinary coefficients use `coefplot()` |
| Plot coefficient paths across quantiles | [`pf.qplot()`](/reference/report.qplot.qmd) | `(figure, axes_array)`; unpack before saving |
| Inspect treatment or outcome histories before estimation | [`pf.panelview()`](/reference/did.visualize.panelview.qmd) | Matplotlib axes |

```{python}
figure = pf.coefplot(models, plot_backend="matplotlib")
```

Save a Matplotlib figure with `figure.savefig("coefficients.png")`. For
quantile paths, use `figure, axes = pf.qplot(quantile_models)`. See each plotting
page for size units, labels, existing axes, and backend-specific customization.

For additional runnable recipes, see [regression tables](/tutorials/regression-tables.qmd), and
[model storage](/reference-guide/model-storage.qmd).
